title: Bidirectional A* in Rathmines: Faster Paths!
description: Watch Bidirectional A* explore Dublin street intersections from both ends of a route. The visualization shows how two informed searches meet to dramatically reduce work on real-world map graphs.
ig_caption:
🚦 Dublin (Rathmines) street map… but make it algorithmic. 

🧠 Bidirectional A* runs two A* searches simultaneously: one forward from the start node and one backward from the goal node (on the street-map graph). Each side uses a heuristic (like straight-line distance) to stay focused, while the two frontiers expand until they connect—often cutting search expansions compared to a single-direction A*. 

🗺️ Real-world twist: streets become a weighted graph where intersections are nodes and road segments are edges. Because the graph is sparse and irregular (one-ways, varying block lengths, connectivity), Bidirectional A*’s “meet-in-the-middle” strategy shines as both search waves converge along plausible routes. 

✅ Want a version using traffic-aware weights (time instead of distance)? Comment your preferred weighting model. If this helped, tap ❤️ and share with a fellow coder! 

🎬 Full replay shows the expanding frontiers and the final stitched path—watch how the meeting point forms.
fb_caption:
🚕 Pathfinding on a real street map—Dublin (Rathmines) edition! 

Bidirectional A* is a graph search that runs two informed searches at once: one from the start and one from the goal. When the two frontiers meet, the algorithm reconstructs the route, often exploring far fewer intersections than classic one-way A*. 

If you enjoy learning from visual algorithms, share this post with someone who loves maps and coding—and tell us whether you’d like weights for distance or travel time.
yt_description:
Bidirectional A* on real-world street maps in Dublin (Rathmines)! 🚦 Two-way informed graph search meets in the middle to find faster routes. In this visualization, we convert streets into a weighted graph (intersections = nodes, road segments = edges), then run Bidirectional A* with a heuristic to guide expansions from both the start and goal. 

Keywords: bidirectional A*, pathfinding visualization, shortest path, graph search, A* algorithm, real map routing, coding reel.
